assessment_boundary: Portfolio publication readiness only; not an academic or vendor assessment, Microsoft assessment, course grade, certification, legal opinion, security audit, or proof of professional qualification.

rubric.finding: Claims are well classified and bounded; lesson-label and static-workflow wording is accurate. Chronology, professional identity, authorship allocation, and origin or non-copying statements remain declarations.
Material claims link directly to results, tests, provenance, QA artifacts, projects, and pinned sources; all local links passed validation.
The one-command standard-library check passed, all 16 project tests and the repository test passed, and all five saved results matched current execution.
Each demonstration maps a technical concept to a recognizable legal workflow and states a human-review boundary, but examples are toy-scale and have no qualified external legal evaluation.
The repository specifically discloses human direction, substantial AI drafting, dates, prior materials, and limitations; the historical role allocation remains self-declared.

Synthetic fixtures, privacy blocking, authorization flags, human review, attribution, and upstream licensing are clear. Controls are illustrative, local-kit provenance and license terms are unresolved beyond disclosure, and no real-world security, fairness, or impact assessment exists.

claims.finding: No external employment, professional-qualification, or bar-admission evidence is included.
The learning statement correctly labels the review as a learner declaration and disclaims a Microsoft credential or grade.
Lessons 1 through 24 appear exactly once, all 24 pinned upstream URLs resolved, and the README accurately calls the headings lesson labels.
Five runnable source, data, test, and result packages exist; their date and post-review chronology are self-declared.
6 of 6 authored synthetic routes match expected queues.
The regenerated six-item test metrics are 33.3 percent for the keyword baseline and 66.7 percent for the perceptron.
Two constructed rectangles on one synthetic page produce mean best IoU 1.0 and 22 reported redacted pixels.
Four synthetic clauses produce 100 percent routing, 91.7 percent entity-field accuracy, correct retrieval, and one retained written-date error.

Six synthetic requests route as expected; the marked privacy request is blocked, external action receives a flag, all outcomes require human review, and the three-role sequence is a static specification.
Imports, runner behavior, regenerated outputs, and passing tests support the claim in this review environment.
The role split is transparently documented but cannot independently authenticate who directed or generated each artifact.
Included fixtures are visibly designed and contain no apparent client or real-person record; their origin and the absence of undisclosed source material remain declarations.
The pinned upstream curriculum is available under the MIT License, and repository wording clearly disclaims endorsement, credential, official assignments, and grade.
Earlier local sources are unavailable for comparison; the repository transparently avoids claiming independent provenance and discloses missing local-kit license metadata.
The response log records the earlier assessment and wording fixes; the fresh review independently reaches the same PASS, PUBLISH, 93 out of 100 result.
The artifacts do not support these claims, and the repository expressly avoids making them.

lesson_evidence_boundary.note: For lessons 20 and 23, tests cover instructions, skill routing, and a static ordered workflow description, not an LLM or live multi-agent runtime.

non_blocking_improvements: After publication, expose a hosted CI result and retain commit history for state and chronology verification.
Link a suitable public professional source only if professional qualification is intended as an independently verifiable claim.
Add source-owner confirmation or license evidence if stronger claims about the local kit's origin or adaptation rights are needed.
